name: U.S. Bank Home Mortgage
notes: Researched from public usbank.com mortgage pages and knowledge-base articles only. Digital banking: mortgage > View, pay & manage > Payment (Monthly payment or Other payment: Additional principal / Additional escrow; optional future Payment date; Submit payment > Authorize payment). Autopay: Enroll in Autopay below the Payment date field, Modify Autopay, Unenroll from Autopay; not available while past due; draws from checking or savings on the date chosen (engine models due-date drafting). Paperless: Profile & settings > Paperless preferences (one statement period to take effect). Phone 800-365-7772 automated or banker (same-day credit). Mail: ATTN Payment Processing, 3751 Airpark Drive, Owensboro KY 42301; allow 7+ business days. No fees and no grace/late fee details on these pages (not modelled). Card payments not described (bank-only inferred). Sign-in is a username (inferred).

sources.title: How do I make a mortgage payment?

autopay.note: Autopay cannot be set up or changed while the loan is past due.

help.title: Ways to pay your mortgage
paragraphs: In online banking or the app, select your mortgage, choose View, pay & manage, then Payment. Choose Monthly payment or Other payment (Additional principal and/or Additional escrow), pick the payment account and an optional future Payment date, then Submit payment and Authorize payment.

By phone, call 800-365-7772 and say make a payment; payments are credited the same day (next business day on weekends and holidays). By mail, send the statement slip and check with your loan number to U.S. Bank Home Mortgage, ATTN: Payment Processing, 3751 Airpark Drive, Owensboro, KY 42301, and allow at least seven business days. You can also pay at a branch.

help.title: Mortgage autopay
paragraphs: Autopay draws your monthly payment from a checking or savings account on the date you choose, and you can set it up, change it or cancel it in online banking or the mobile app. You are told by mail when the first payment is drawn; a draft that falls on a weekend or holiday is credited the next business day.
You cannot enroll in or change autopay while your loan is past due.
steps: Select your mortgage, then View, pay & manage.
Choose Payment at the top of the page.
Select Enroll in Autopay below the Payment date field (or Modify Autopay / Unenroll from Autopay).
Review the terms, check the box and select Enroll.

help.title: Paperless statements
paragraphs: In online banking go to Profile & settings, then Paperless preferences; in the app use Statements & docs. The change takes one full statement period to take effect.

help.title: Pay by phone
paragraphs: Call 800-365-7772. Say make a payment or pay my escrow, then give the bank account number, routing number and amount. The system reads the details back; say Yes to submit. Bankers are available Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. CT and Saturday 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. CT.

help.title: Enroll in, change or cancel mortgage autopay
paragraphs: From the dashboard select your mortgage (View, pay & manage, or View and manage if you have other accounts), then choose Payment. Select Enroll in Autopay under the Payment date field, complete the form, accept the terms and select Enroll. Use Modify Autopay to change it or Unenroll from Autopay to stop it.
The confirmation page shows the date of the first payment your setup or change applies to; the current month's payment may not change.

extra.intent: A U.S. Bank Home Mortgage borrower whose loan is past due wants to enroll in autopay right now. Using the help pages, explain whether they can. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: No. Autopay cannot be set up or changed while the loan is past due; bring the loan current first.

extra.intent: Using the U.S. Bank help pages, find how long a switch to paperless mortgage statements takes to take effect. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: It takes one full statement period.
